project.title: Netflix Is a Joke: The Festival
project.medium: festival campaign identity and event visual system
project.format: Copy-led identity spanning promotional campaign, trailer, out-of-home takeovers, and main-stage graphics

why: A strong campaign reference because one copy-led visual grammar carries an unusually large comedy programme from promotion into a live event. PORTO ROCHA combines wood-type-inspired typography, dimensional containers, and a deliberately self-aware voice so the system can accommodate many performers while remaining recognizable in trailer, out-of-home, and stage-scale applications.

artDirection.title: The campaign voice is a visual ingredient
artDirection.study: PORTO ROCHA describes a dry, self-aware persona that can promote talent while poking fun at itself, turning over-articulated asides and comedy-culture references into a consistent campaign voice.
artDirection.reuse: Define a constrained verbal persona alongside the visual system when a campaign needs many changing messages to still read as one world.

artDirection.title: Bold type carries the high-volume programme
artDirection.study: The case study identifies bold, wood-type-inspired typography across copy and logo as the identity's core, helping the campaign cut through a media-saturated Los Angeles landscape.
artDirection.reuse: Give the recognition-bearing type treatment enough weight and contrast to survive talent swaps, dense schedules, and distant outdoor viewing.

artDirection.title: One graphic device can flex from announcement to event
artDirection.study: Dimensional graphic containers support the typography and provide a repeatable visual device rather than a separate illustrated hero for each performer.
artDirection.reuse: Use a small family of original containers or frames to make variable copy and talent content feel authored by one campaign system.

channelFormats.title: Promotion and live experience share one identity
channelFormats.notes: The studio explicitly designed for continuity from the promotional campaign through the festival experience, despite a lineup spanning 130 comedians and more than 280 events.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Keep the type, copy voice, and dimensional-container grammar stable while programme information changes by performer, venue, and date.
channelFormats.reuse: Treat operational campaign content as a variable layer, not a reason to invent a separate graphic style for each announcement.

channelFormats.title: Comedy voice scales to city-size placements
channelFormats.notes: The official case names larger-than-life out-of-home takeovers as part of the campaign rollout.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Favor short, high-contrast copy and an unmistakable typographic silhouette for distant or brief reads.
channelFormats.reuse: Test a campaign's core line and lockup at outdoor-reading distance before adding secondary detail.

channelFormats.title: The same graphic language reaches the main stage
channelFormats.notes: Colorful main-stage graphics extend the campaign from media placements into the live festival environment.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Retain the shared type and dimensional grammar while simplifying detail for large, time-based stage views.
channelFormats.reuse: Plan a scale-specific stage composition that remains visibly connected to the static campaign without forcing a poster layout onto a screen.

assets.notes: The source identifies wood-type-inspired typography and Midnight Sans by Colophon; no type files or source artwork are included in this library.
assets.reuse: License an appropriate typeface or use an original typographic treatment rather than reproducing the source's lettering.

assets.notes: The case describes dimensional containers as an identity component that supports copy and logo; the proprietary forms are not reproduced locally.
assets.reuse: Create original geometric frames with an explicit depth and lighting rule when a campaign needs an adaptable supporting layer.

motion.title: Dimensionality becomes an announcement motion principle
motion.notes: Netflix and Panic Studio used the identity's dimensional element in a trailer that brings the logo to life.
motion.fallback: Keep the wordmark and campaign copy fully legible in a still frame; offer a static key visual or low-motion crossfade where animation is unavailable or unwanted.

implementation.format: Festival campaign reference connecting a copy-led visual identity to programme promotion, motion announcement, outdoor media, and stage graphics
implementation.notes: PORTO ROCHA's first-party case study documents the event scale, campaign-to-event continuity, typography, dimensional containers, trailer collaboration, out-of-home, stage graphics, and named creative credits. The source supports reusable principles only; original local previews must not embed or reproduce Netflix, PORTO ROCHA, Panic Studio, performer, photography, or font assets.
